findings.summary: The new tests write and run executables in-process, the ETXTBSY race this repository forbids in test code. The suite is flaky and failed in this verification.
findings.evidence: The first run of `cargo test -p athena-cli slot_exec` failed: "cargo: running /tmp/.tmpouhzLq/bin/cargo: Text file busy (os error 26)", exit 127 instead of 0, in unslotted_subcommands_link_nothing_and_touch_no_slot_directory. Reruns passed. crates/athena-testkit/tests/no_in_process_exec_writes.rs requires stand-ins to be written with athena_testkit::write_executable, which athena-cli already has as a dev-dependency. The scan misses these tests only because slot_exec.rs is on EXEMPT with the reason "writes scripts with a chosen mode, some not executable, and never runs them", which the new tests make false. Fix: write the fake cargo with athena_testkit::write_executable.
findings.location: crates/athena-cli/src/slot_exec.rs (tests: Fixture::job, std::fs::write plus set_permissions(from_mode(0o755)) of bin/cargo, then run() executes it)

findings.summary: Soundness: the wrapper links the slot but never runs the workspace-output clean that the scheme requires after each command, so the producer's workspace-crate output builds up in the shared slot.
findings.evidence: docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md section 5.3 step 3 says that after each command `cargo clean -p <each workspace member>` runs in the slot, and that this "is what stops the slot growing by one set of workspace crates per job". The checks do this through clean_slot_target / slots::clean_workspace_output. The wrapper drops the link and leaves the producer's workspace output in <state>/build-slots/<n>/target. Nothing removes that output when the job closes: before, it sat in the job's private directory, which is deleted at close. Only a later local check in the same slot cleans it, and section 5.1 says most jobs (4 of 5 sampled) run no local check. For an operator whose disk fills, the growth moves from a per-job directory into a permanent one. Simpler, more correct alternative: after the child exits, call athena_core::slots::clean_workspace_output on the slot target, with the reset-on-failure the checks use, before releasing the slot.

findings.summary: The slot target layout is re-derived from a hard-coded name instead of the state layout's own function. The directory is also made without the CACHEDIR.TAG that make_target_dir writes.
findings.evidence: `shim.slots_dir.parent()?.join("build-slots")` duplicates StateDir::build_slots_dir / slot_target. It silently diverges if either layout changes. std::fs::create_dir_all omits the CACHEDIR.TAG; state.rs says `cargo clean` refuses a directory without it. The checks' prepare_slot_target adds the tag later, so this is not breaking today. The reading said the directory is "created if missing, as make_target_dir does". Alternative: pass the slot target directory to the wrapper through the CargoShim environment, or share the layout function and make_target_dir.

findings.summary: An absent CARGO_TARGET_DIR, or a shim directory with no parent, silently runs unlinked with no warning, contrary to the reading.
findings.evidence: The reading says an absent CARGO_TARGET_DIR "means a warning on stderr and cargo runs unlinked". The code returns None through `?` without printing anything.

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The reading describes the job as "link, run cargo, drop the link" and names checks.rs link_slot_target as the model. But the design it builds on (agent-and-build-slots.md section 5.3 step 3, and the checks' clean_slot_target that follows every linked command) also cleans workspace-crate output from the slot after each command. The reading leaves out that step without listing it as out of scope (only size-limit deletion is excluded). So the change brings the producer into the warm slot without the clean that keeps the slot from growing per job.

summary: The candidate fails verification for two reasons. It does link the producer's build directory to the slot's warm target directory during slotted cargo commands, and all seven criteria are met in substance. First, the new tests are flaky: my first run of `cargo test -p athena-cli slot_exec` failed with "Text file busy". The tests write the fake cargo themselves and then run it, the race this repository bans in test code; `athena_testkit::write_executable` is the required way. The ban's checker misses these tests only because it exempts slot_exec.rs on the grounds that its scripts are never run, which the new tests make false. Reruns, including with one test thread, passed. Second, the approach has a design gap. After each command, the checks clean the workspace crates' output out of the slot, and the design names that as what stops the slot growing with every job. The wrapper skips this step. The producer's output then builds up in a directory nothing deletes, which works against the disk problem this change is meant to solve. Two smaller issues: the slot path is rebuilt from a hard-coded name rather than taken from the state layout, and the wrapper makes the directory without the CACHEDIR.TAG file that `cargo clean` needs. A missing CARGO_TARGET_DIR is also skipped silently, though the reading promised a warning. Fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in CI (run 42384396530). Only CHANGELOG.md and slot_exec.rs changed.
